correctness.rationale: For each cycle C_n (n>=3) the intersection closure of maximal independent sets containing an independent S is S plus vertices whose two distance-2 neighbors lie in S (n>=5); any adjacent pair has empty object extension and closure V. Minimum nonclosed-premise lower bound forces all n adjacent pairs plus distinct forcing pairs (n>=6), with exactly four forcing pairs at n=8; n=3,4,5 give 3,4,5 rules, others 2n. All minimum displayed bases are one-pass because the closure lemma acts on original premises. Shattering upper bound uses cyclic spacings: two short gaps of 2 require a long gap >=4 between them through any 3-gap chain; hence n>=3k-1. Lower construction uses chosen vertices at gaps >=3 except at most one gap 2, choosing neighboring helpers to omit any selected vertex, and extends to a maximal independent set. Exact independent exhaustive script recomputed maximal independent sets, nonclosed minimal premises, one-pass closures, all traces for every subset n=3..13, reproducing B_n,D_n. This finite test is not an all-n proof.
